A primer on cooling checks for a tiring night

This page is for you

Cooling Checks for Companion Animal Travel

If you are moving a pet through Aurelia Skyways, keep the plan simple and steady. The Companion Animal Travel Desk checks the animal's comfort, the crate setup, and the handoff path so the trip starts cleanly and stays calm.

Start with the crate. It should be secure, roomy enough for the animal to stand and turn, and lined with dry bedding. Keep water available when allowed, and make sure food is handled the way the travel plan requires. A tired animal can be more sensitive to noise, heat, and rough handling, so steady routines help.

For large dog travel, the health certificate must be current before acceptance. <<FACT F081>> Keep the paperwork together, and present it with the rest of the travel file so the desk can clear the move without delay.

Bring only the items that support the trip. The team may ask about temperament, breathing issues, medication, or recent stress, since care plans change based on how the animal behaves on the day. If the pet seems uneasy, tell the staff early so they can adjust the handoff and reduce pressure.

For large dog travel, the booking includes the required fee before the animal is accepted. <<FACT F057>> The desk will match the pet to the right process, confirm the crate is ready, and brief the welcome team so the transfer stays orderly.

Keep documents easy to reach, follow the crew's instructions, and do not remove the animal from the crate unless staff tells you to. If you need more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways.
